blocks.text: The chapter contrasts misleading teaching with the stable instruction Timothy has received. Its description of people entering households and taking advantage of burdened women is polemical: the point is their exploitation and their resistance to truth, not a general judgment on women. Against this, Timothy’s lifelong knowledge of the sacred writings is presented as a source of wisdom directed toward salvation through faith in Christ Jesus. Scripture is then described as useful for teaching, exposing error, correction, and training in righteousness.

The opening warning about “the last days” is applied to the letter’s own audience through a catalogue of destructive conduct, including an outward form of godliness that lacks its power. The comparison with Jannes and Jambres—traditional names for Pharaoh’s magicians—portrays opposition to truth as ultimately exposed. Paul also sets his own teaching and endured persecutions alongside this warning, before concluding that Scripture equips the person of God completely for every good work.

sections.title: Reading the Warnings and the Scriptures

blocks.text: Among surviving manuscripts, Codex Sinaiticus includes 2 Timothy. Codex Vaticanus, by contrast, ends before the Pastoral Epistles, so it is not a witness to this letter.
